CORRECTED AT THE PRE-COMMIT GATE. This AC was first scored `met` on evidence that was not evidence: three tests seeded a `kind: "tool_call"` step, which server/ws-handler.ts:242-264 never persists — it filters those steps out and folds them into the assistant as `toolCalls[]` (architecture.md Implementation Constraint 4 describes exactly this). So `turnHasToolCall` scanned for a kind production does not produce, AC-UX-6's mandatory 'report reconciliation as unavailable' was DEAD CODE, and the panel would have shown a reconciliation for a tool-loop turn whose usage covers only the last of several requests — the exact harm the AC exists to prevent. Found by the cold Stage-2 reviewer, not the warm one. NOW GENUINELY MET: turnHasToolCall detects a tool_result step or an assistant step with non-empty toolCalls[], in addition to the legacy kind; turn-scoping preserved. Lead-verified directly against the real functions on three shapes — production merged: detected; legacy tour: detected; tool-free turn after a tool turn: NOT detected (no over-fire). Tests now seed both persisted shapes, each labelled with which it represents and why both exist. Three figures + label wording unchanged and still asserted.

frontend_typecheck_baseline.reason: The mutation-remediation round added `import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach } from 'vitest'` to tests/unit/chat.test.ts, which it was legitimately editing. Without it, its 10 new test blocks would have added ~28 NEW type errors, violating the binding 0-net-new rule; the same import incidentally resolved 20 pre-existing errors of the identical kind. Every sibling test file already uses explicit imports and contributes zero errors, so this follows the codebase's own convention. Flagged rather than decided silently. architecture.md Constraint 9's pinned figure of 201 is now stale — future comparisons should use 181.
frontend_typecheck_baseline.framing_correction: The lead initially recorded this as the OPPOSITE call from the S3 round (which deliberately avoided importing `vi` to preserve 201). The Stage-1 reviewer pushed back and is right: both rounds applied the SAME rule — don't perturb the pinned baseline gratuitously; when the work forces a perturbation, take the direction that follows repo convention and record it. The actions differed because the constraints did. In S3 the import was OPTIONAL (plain consts achieved the same result; the change was cosmetic), so moving the baseline would have bought nothing. Here it was FORCED (without it the new tests broke zero-net-new), and no option preserved 201. Same principle, different constraint — not a reversal.

mutation_gate_notes.static_mutant_ceiling: 15 of server/tokenizer.ts's 40 live mutants are flagged static:true — the vitest runner imports the module once and activates mutants per-test afterwards, so a module-level initializer's mutants never run. They put a hard ~0.95 ceiling on that module regardless of test quality. `ignoreStatic: true` would remove them from the denominator but would make future deltas incomparable to this baseline; left unset deliberately.

open_items_to_backlog.reason: A gap-closing test pins a provably-equivalent mutant and its justification is inaccurate. It annotates `__preTokenizeForTests('') returns []` as guarding a branch 'unreachable via tokenize()', but splitOnSpecialTokens early-returns [text] UNFILTERED when a vocabulary declares no special tokens, so preTokenize('') IS reachable — and separately the guard cannot change observable behaviour, since ''.match(QWEN2_SPLIT_REGEX) is null and the ?? [] fallback already yields []. Harmless, but it is the one test in the mutation batch whose value is coverage rather than discrimination. Either drop the test and the redundant guard together, or keep it and correct the comment to say the branch is reachable but behaviourally equivalent.

PRE-EXISTING WIRE BEHAVIOR, deliberately not fixed inside this epic. toOllamaMessages never reads step.toolCalls, while its sibling toOpenAIMessages (shared/openai-format.ts:105-122) handles both the legacy and merged shapes. Since ws-handler persists the merged format, the real second-iteration request to Ollama DROPS the tool-call announcement entirely. Surfaced when the merged shape was added to the contract-test generators: the 'announces every tool the assistant actually called' property genuinely fails and is marked `it.fails` with a comment naming it — the suite stays green without masking it. Fix by mirroring openai-format.ts's assistant branch. Out of scope here because changing what we send to Ollama is not a thing to do at a feature epic's commit gate.

Second half of F7, deliberately deferred: surface the tokenize.error reason (the wire already carries `unsupported_provider`) instead of collapsing every rejection into generic 'failed' wording. The provider gate added at the pre-commit gate makes this path structurally unreachable for non-Ollama conversations, and broader reason-surfacing would mean refactoring token-view.ts's whole failure-reason discipline.

'Reconciliation for the last completed turn' can mislabel. A thinking-only response (assistant content empty -> compactSteps drops the step and its usage) or a stopped/errored stream leaves the most recent turn with no usage, so findLastUsageStep silently reconciles an EARLIER turn under that heading. Separately, editing/deleting/reordering steps after a turn completes (all supported in the transcript UI) leaves steps[0..i) no longer equal to the request that produced promptEvalCount, and the figure drifts with no notice. Candidate fix: name the reconciled turn in the heading, and/or snapshot the sent message list's hash on the usage-bearing step at chat.done.

'resolves an equal-rank tie deterministically' pins a state real merge tables cannot produce (ranks are unique line indices), so its oracle is the implementation's `<` rather than any reference. Survivor-chasing rather than behavioral. Drop it, or reframe as 'a merge table with duplicate ranks still terminates and joins to the input'.

The preview panel's Ollama gate keys on the provider ID, not ProviderConfig.type — a latent violation of architecture.md Boundary Rule 4 ('gate on ProviderConfig.type, never on provider name'), the very rule this epic established and was already burned by in S3. ModelInfo does not surface the type to the frontend at all (llm-router.ts sets provider = config.id at :224/:245/:256). Harmless in the shipped default config, where the Ollama provider's id happens to be 'ollama'. Fails in both directions otherwise: a second Ollama host (id 'ollama-remote', type 'ollama') hides the panel for a genuine Ollama conversation, and an openai-compat provider given id 'ollama' would show Ollama filtering and a prompt_eval_count label. Fix: add providerType: config.type to ModelInfo at all three sites, mirror it on OllamaModel in src/types/chat.ts, gate on that. RECORDED AGAINST validation-provider-type-gate rather than leaving the concept closed clean — the gate currently LOOKS compliant, which is the part that matters for whoever adds a second Ollama provider.

The provenance cleanup is partial: ~13 workflow finding-ID prefixes (S3-F2/F9/F12/F13, S3-R1/R2/R3/R6, S3-F3) remain in production source outside the four files that were stripped. In every case the surrounding sentence is durable reasoning that must stay — server/tokenizer.ts:405's 'delete by key AND identity — the LRU can re-register this key with a newer in-flight promise' is exactly what a future reader needs — and only the short ID prefix is workflow history. The codebase now reads as if the rule applies in some files and not others. Either strip the remaining IDs keeping every sentence, or restore them in the four stripped files; the cost of either is small, the cost of two conventions is that neither reads as intentional.

turnHasToolCall over-fires conservatively on one shape: a single-request turn whose assistant announced a tool the dispatcher could not execute (ws-handler.ts:266-283, executableToolCalls.length === 0 -> chat.done with assistant{toolCalls, usage}). There usage covers the whole (only) request so reconciliation would be valid, but the panel reports unavailable. AC-UX-6's literal wording ('a turn whose steps include any tool_call') mandates exactly this, so it is spec-compliant — recorded only so the behaviour is not rediscovered as a bug. No action taken.
